conflict_topics: management of wet laundry during cooking
dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation is natural and problem-focused; participants state concrete constraints (work calls, clothes, wet laundry) and propose schedule-based compromises.

Some needless repetition appears (multiple identical or repeated turns by Agent C: "Friday's laundry will still be out on Saturday." and "And I have to move it all in there..." repeated), contributing to a moderate repetition score.
Speakers remain consistent about the setting and constraints; offers and counter-offers are tangible (times and temporary storage).
evaluation.final_reason: Parties agreed on one concrete mitigation: D proposed Sunday evening as a cooking time (Turn 29: "Okay. What about Sunday evening then? Is your laundry taken in by then?") and the others accepted it (Turn 30: C: "Yeah, it's in by then. Sunday evening works." Turn 31: A: "Sunday evening is good." Turn 32: B: "Sunday works for me."). This constitutes a partial compromise: D retains one weekday/weekend slot to cook while A–C obtained a guaranteed time when laundry won't be exposed. The remaining substantive issue — the second weekly cooking slot — was explicitly left open (Turn 33: "So that's one day. What about the second time during the week?").
position_change_notes: Agent A: moved from asking for a ban on strong smells to proposing a specific compromise day (Saturday) and later accepted Sunday (Turn 5, Turn 31).
Agent D: initially defended the cooking as important (Turn 4) but then showed flexibility by offering Saturday, then offering notice and accommodations, and proposing Sunday (Turns 6, 14, 29).

Agent C: consistently highlighted the practical constraint of wet laundry and resisted accommodations requiring moving wet clothes; ultimately accepted Sunday when it fit laundry timing (Turn 10, Turn 30).
Agent B: registered the smell problem early and accepted the compromise once a workable day was proposed (Turn 2, Turn 8, Turn 32).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A raises a request to stop strong-smelling cooking because it interferes with work: "It's just that I work from home... The smell gets very strong..." Agent B supports the complaint about smell in clothes: "My room is the one next to the kitchen. The smell gets into all my clothes." An incompatibility is introduced but no opposing position has yet been voiced.

Agent D voices the origin and cultural importance of the cooking: "Sorry, I know the smell is strong. That's my fish curry. It's the food I grew up with." This expresses an interest that conflicts with A/B/C's request to avoid strong smells, turning the complaint into a clear substantive disagreement.

Agent A offers a scheduling compromise: "What if you cook it on Saturdays? I'm usually not here then." Agent D responds positively to the idea but raises a further constraint: "Saturday could work. But what about you two? The laundry, your clothes." The conflict softens into a negotiable scheduling trade-off.

Agent B accepts the proposed Saturday compromise: "Saturday is fine. As long as I close my door, it's okay." Agent D seeks Agent C's view: "Agent C, what about the laundry?" Several parties accept the idea, but C's position is not yet known, so some disagreement remains.

Agent C objects to Saturday because their laundry will still be out: "Friday's laundry will still be out on Saturday." This undermines the Saturday compromise and reintroduces a clear opposing practical constraint.

Agent D offers a mitigation: "Okay. What if I let you know before I start cooking? Then you can take your laundry in first." Agent C responds with a practical problem: "But it's still wet. Where am I supposed to put it?" The substantive incompatibility remains unresolved.

Agent D proposes an accommodation: "You can hang it in my room while I'm cooking." C repeats the wet-laundry problem earlier raised. D's offer softens the conflict (an accommodation is offered), but C's objection to the burden persists.

Agent C objects to the proposed accommodation as impractical: "And I have to move it all in there, and then move it all back out again every time?" This reiteration maintains the unresolved practical disagreement about handling wet laundry.

Agent D attempts another scheduling workaround: "Okay, then what time on Saturday is good for you? I can cook before you put your laundry out." Agent C responds that the laundry is already hanging on Saturday: "I do my laundry on Friday night. It's already hanging there on Saturday." The proposed workaround is undermined; the substantive conflict persists.

Agent D offers a different time: "Okay. What about Sunday evening then? Is your laundry taken in by then?" Agent C confirms a scheduling possibility but clarifies constraints: "Like I said, my laundry from Friday is already out on Saturday. So there's no 'before' time." The conflict shifts toward a narrower scheduling disagreement and D proposes a concrete alternative.

Agent C accepts Sunday: "Yeah, it's in by then. Sunday evening works." Agent A also agrees: "Sunday evening is good." A common time for one weekly cooking slot is jointly accepted, reducing but not eliminating the overall conflict (the second weekly cooking remains open).

Agent B also accepts Sunday: "Sunday works for me." Agent C immediately raises the remaining issue: "So that's one day. What about the second time during the week?" The parties have reached mutual agreement on one cooking slot (Sunday) but the second weekly occurrence remains unresolved.

substantive_insights: The core tension is scheduling vs. cultural food practices: D values cooking a culturally important dish while others bear smell-related harms to work and laundry.
Laundry timing is the decisive practical constraint: Saturday cooking clashes with C's laundry schedule, so moving to Sunday removes that specific conflict.
Accommodation proposals focused on sequencing (cook before laundry) or temporary relocation of wet laundry, but the latter imposes an additional burden that C resists.
Resolution proceeded by narrowing the problem (agree on one slot) rather than solving the full frequency issue, leaving a remaining negotiation over the second weekly cooking.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 12 because the final status is partially_resolved.
